title: Stream anchoring: three messages and forty

tasks.title: Three messages: paints from the top

messages.text: does the stream start at the top?
It should. A conversation with three messages in a full-height panel paints from the top with empty space below it, the way every chat does.
and a long one?

tasks.title: Forty messages: scrolled to the end

messages.text: where does the board live when eight agents are running?
As a left column, 236 px wide. Composition A: the panels tile beside it and reflow when you close one.
what does a panel wear as chrome?
Two rows. The title row folds the status into itself, then the tab row. Arrangement 2 in the mockup.
what happens at 296 px?
The status group yields: the zoom glyph first, then the age, then the verb, until the title has 40% of the row.
why does the zoom glyph go first?
It is a duplicate. Zoom is a row of the menu and it has a key of its own, so the glyph costs 20 px for nothing.
does Done ever yield?
No. Done and the menu are how the panel is operated at all; an anonymous panel beats an inoperable one.
what about the plan strip?
It goes before all three. Ninety pixels of strip on a 350 px panel costs more than the other rungs together.
how are the blocks spaced?
Ten pixels between blocks, two between a role label and the body it heads, twelve of region padding.
what was wrong before?
The meta row sat in the flow under every block, invisible, and charged each one about 27 px of dead air.
where did the meta row go?
Over the block's own label line, at the right. The label is two short words at the left, so the two never meet.
does the composer still wrap?
No. The pill is one line at rest and the placeholder ellipsises rather than folding onto a second.
when do the key hints show?
Only where the field is at least 420 px wide. Below that they eat the field they are annotating.
and the meta line?
Segments drop from the right - quota, branch, access, effort - and the provider and the model never drop.
why keep the provider and the model?
They say where the draft is going. Everything else on that line is reachable from a selector or the menu.
is this scrolled to the end?
It is. A top-aligned list has no implicit end anchor, so the timeline asks for one past the last row.
what did the bottom alignment do?
It set a negative scroll offset when the content was short and pinned the last row to the panel floor.
how is follow kept?
By the visible range on the wheel event, and by a pixel test against the scrollbar's own maximum offset.
what is the re-arm band?
Forty pixels above the true content bottom. Strict, so reading history does not re-arm live follow.
does the estimate still match?
Yes - the row height counts the label, its gap, the body and the block gap, and nothing that has left the flow.
what proves any of this?
The renders. Every claim in the report was read off a PNG rather than reasoned about.
and the last message?
This one. If you can read it without scrolling, the stream is anchored at its end.
